name: Jabal
overview: Jabal is a male biblical figure identified as the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock. His unique attribute highlights his role in the early development of nomadic pastoral life. Scripture does not specify his tribe or additional personal details beyond this significant contribution.
namesAndTitles: The name Jabal appears as a proper name in Genesis 4:20. There is no specific meaning or divine origin provided for his name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Jabal is recorded as the son of Lamech and Adah, as inferred from Genesis 4:20. Beyond these parental relationships, Scripture does not provide further familial details.
scriptureSignificance: Jabal's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his pioneering role as the progenitor of nomadic herders and tent dwellers. This positions him as a foundational figure in the development of early human civilization, particularly in the context of pastoral life. His mention underscores the diversification of human occupations following the early generations of mankind.
